expectations.text: Class comment states purpose and thread-safety guarantee
expectations.evidence: Class comment covers mechanism, burst behavior, a usage example, and 'Thread-safe: any number of threads...' including the no-FIFO-fairness caveat.

expectations.text: Every public method declaration has a contract comment
expectations.evidence: Constructor, Acquire, TryAcquire documented; capacity() is a trivial accessor legitimately left bare per the guide.

expectations.text: Acquire documents blocking; TryAcquire documents true/false and nothing-consumed-on-failure
expectations.evidence: Acquire: blocks, n>capacity would block forever, lock not held while waiting. TryAcquire: 'otherwise consumes nothing and returns false. Never blocks.'

expectations.text: Units documented for rates and durations
expectations.evidence: 'refills continuously at tokens_per_second', rate_ '// Refill rate in tokens per second.'

expectations.text: .cc explains implementation choices without duplicating .h contracts
expectations.evidence: .cc comments explain lazy refill vs background thread, exact-sleep vs polling, and the concurrent re-check loop — none restate the .h contract.

expectations.text: No restating comments; no Author lines; consistent // style
expectations.evidence: All comments carry intent; the one inline comment ('// Start full so initial bursts are not throttled.') explains a why.
Usage example: TokenBucket(/*tokens_per_second=*/100.0, /*capacity=*/100.0); no unannotated literal call sites in the code.
